title: Lee plans to publish Lester's songs to get royalties to his family
summary: Lee says companies exploit deceased musicians without accounting to the estate, and says he will copyright Lester's songs in his Flipside publishing company for Lester Jr.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I'll tell you something on this tape -- and then I'm gonna close out with this. But let me tell you something. I'm in the recording business, right? I think and I see where musicians that are deceased, I think it's just criminal what the record companies do and the people that have the masters, what they get away with, by putting these people's music out and with no accounting to the estate, no accounting to anything.

So there's a fellow who's getting ready to do a thing on Lester -- do all of Lester's solos as they did Charlie Parker's thing -- and all of the songs that Lester has written is in to this publishing company. I'm gonna take all of the songs and put them in my publishing company; the same songs with the same arrangements, and I'm gonna make them come after me. Because I'm gonna get them for

Lester Junior. But I'm gonna make them fight for it. So I'm gonna copyright the same things, you know? So I just wanted -- you don't have to keep this for posterity, but I mean that, because it's an unfair situation.

You see everybody has something out on him now, and his family gets nothing. Because they don't understand, and they do this in the record business all the time. They don't get an accounting for the music they've written, they don't get accounting for the performances -- so they can tell Mary or Lester, 'Oh, I paid him when he did this. There was no royalty deal.'

But there's no such thing as no royalty deal. Now that I'm in the record business, I know that when a person performs and if they are the artist, there is a royalty deal someplace. So if you don't have one now, you can make one. And that's really the way I feel about it, because I'm going to take the same songs, the same arrangements, and I'm going to copyright them and I'm gonna put them in my publishing company, which is called Flipside, when you see Flipside, you'll know -- that I will get the money and I will give it to Lester's son and his wife.
But I'll make them come after it. Because I know how to fight them about it. But see, they don't have a clue. You got to fight them about it.
